items.title: Better Call Saul：词汇与搭配积累
items.body:
# Better Call Saul：词汇与搭配积累

## S01E01

| 单词／搭配 | 本句意思 | 原句（时间码） |
|---|---|---|
| spur | n. 马刺；骑马靴后用来催马的小装置（片头电视） | Look, he's even got the spurs on the back of his boots.（00:02:59–00:03:02） |
| allegation | n. 尚未证实的指控／说法；false allegations 不实指控 | Don't let false allegations bully you into an unfair fight.（00:05:14–00:05:18） |
| charge | n. 刑事指控；此处不是费用／充电 | No charge is too big for me.（00:05:22–00:05:24） |
| dismiss a case | v. 驳回／终止案件；dismiss 此处不是解雇 | I'll get your case dismissed.（00:05:29–00:05:31） |
| attorney-at-law | n. 律师（正式称谓）；attorney 为美式常用 | Because I'm Saul Goodman, attorney-at-law.（00:05:34–00:05:36） |
| doomed | adj. 注定失败／难逃厄运的；feel doomed 感到无望 | Do you feel doomed?（00:05:44–00:05:46） |
| intimidate | v. 恐吓／使人畏惧；不是 intimate 亲密的 | Have opponents of freedom wrongly intimidated you?（00:05:46–00:05:48） |
| underdeveloped | adj. 发育不充分／发展不足的；此处指少年大脑 | you'll recall that you also had an underdeveloped 19-year-old brain.（00:08:44–00:08:48） |
| accountable | adj. 应负责的；be held accountable for sth. 被要求为某事负责 | Me, personally, I... It... If I were held accountable for some of the stupid decisions I made when I was 19... Oh, boy, wow.（00:08:48–00:08:58） |
| knucklehead | n. 笨蛋／傻瓜（口语，贬义） | Now, these three knuckleheads... And I'm sorry, boys, but that's what you are...（00:09:05–00:09:11） |
| salient | adj. 最重要／突出的；salient facts 关键事实 | However, I would like you to remember two salient facts.（00:09:14–00:09:17） |
| prosecution | n. 控方／公诉方；不是保护 protection | Fact two... Now, the prosecution keeps bandying this term "criminal trespass."（00:09:23–00:09:30） |
| bandy | v. 随口反复提某词／说法；原文 bandying this term | Fact two... Now, the prosecution keeps bandying this term "criminal trespass."（00:09:23–00:09:30） |
| trespass / criminal trespass | n./v. 未经允许进入他人土地或建筑；criminal trespass 刑事非法侵入 | Fact two... Now, the prosecution keeps bandying this term "criminal trespass." Mr. Spinowzo, the property owner, admitted to us that he keeps most portions of his business open to the public both day and night. So, trespassing? That's a bit of a reach... Don't you think, Dave?（00:09:23–00:09:45） |
| portion | n. 一部分／份额；此处指营业场所的区域，不是饭菜的一份 | Mr. Spinowzo, the property owner, admitted to us that he keeps most portions of his business open to the public both day and night.（00:09:30–00:09:39） |
| momentary | adj. 短暂的／一时的；momentary lapse 一时失误 | Call me crazy, but I don't think they deserve to have their bright futures ruined by a momentary, minute,（00:10:01–00:10:08） |
| minute | adj. 极小的／微不足道的；此处不是“分钟” | Call me crazy, but I don't think they deserve to have their bright futures ruined by a momentary, minute, never-to-be-repeated lapse of judgment.（00:10:01–00:10:12） |
| lapse | n. 一时失误；a lapse of judgment 一时判断失误 | Call me crazy, but I don't think they deserve to have their bright futures ruined by a momentary, minute, never-to-be-repeated lapse of judgment.（00:10:01–00:10:12） |
| rolling | 正在录制／开机拍摄（口语）；Are you rolling? 开录了吗？ | - Kenny, Kenny, are you rolling? - Yeah, yeah. Wait a minute.（00:11:14–00:11:16） |
| dumbass | n. 蠢货／傻逼（粗俗骂人话） | Dude, he's dead. They suck it all out, dumbass.（00:11:31–00:11:34） |
| defendant | n. 被告；与 defense 辩护不同 | $700 per defense. No, no, no. "Defendant." "...dant." Three defendants, $2,100, which, by the way, bargain...（00:12:14–00:12:21） |
| try sb. | v. 审理／审判某人；此处不是尝试 | Look, didn't nobody tell you to try all three of them together. One trial... $700.（00:12:29–00:12:34） |
| public defender / P.D. | n. 公设辩护律师，为无力聘律师者提供刑事辩护（美国） | 'Cause it'll be a cold day in hell before I do any more P.D. work for this shitty court!（00:12:35–00:12:39） |
| fumes | n. 浓烈、可能有害的烟气／气味；此处油漆挥发气体 | Uh, unfortunately, our offices are being painted and the fumes are quite horrid.（00:13:23–00:13:27） |
| horrid | adj. 很糟糕／令人不快的；此处指油漆气味 | Uh, unfortunately, our offices are being painted and the fumes are quite horrid.（00:13:23–00:13:27） |
| validate parking | v. 认可停车凭证，使停车费可减免；此处不是证明人可信 | Uh, I'm validated. See the stickers? Well, I see five stickers. You're one shy. It's $3. They gave me... Look. I'm validated for the entire day, okay?（00:14:14–00:14:26） |
| shy | adj. 不足／差一点；one shy 少一个，不是害羞 | You're one shy. It's $3.（00:14:18–00:14:20） |
| swell | adj. 很棒的（较老派口语）；此处带讽刺，不是肿胀 | Well, gee, that's swell. And thank you for restoring my faith in the judicial system.（00:14:33–00:14:39） |
| fuzzy | adj. 模糊／不清楚的；此处指自己不太明白，不是毛茸茸 | Well, I'm just fuzzy as to why you think he needs a lawyer.（00:15:18–00:15:23） |
| reproach | n. 责备／指责；beyond reproach 无可指责 | I mean, Craig, the way you run your office is beyond reproach. Yeah. Yeah. Beyond reproach.（00:15:23–00:15:29） |
| stickler | n. 对规则／细节特别较真的人；a stickler for sth. | Yeah. I'm a stickler, you know, for... He is. He's a stickler with the money. - He's definitely a stickler. - Yeah. Yeah.（00:15:29–00:15:34） |
| wrongdoing | n. 不当／违法行为；innocent of wrongdoing 没有做错／违法 | I mean, he's certainly not guilty of some... Is certainly not. He's innocent of any wrongdoing.（00:15:34–00:15:39） |
| aggravation | n. 烦人的麻烦／恼火；此处不是病情加重 | And frankly, I don't go looking for guilty people to represent. I mean who needs that aggravation, right?（00:15:41–00:15:48） |
| treasury / treasurer | n. 财政部门／公库；treasurer 财务主管，此处县财务官 | And typically, when money goes missing from the county treasury... And the number here is, uh, $1.6 million... Well, that's an accounting... It's an accounting discrepancy. It's a discrepancy, absolutely. But typically, when that happens, the police look at the treasurer.（00:15:52–00:16:08） |
| accounting discrepancy | n. 账目不一致／差异；此处用来淡化资金失踪 | Well, that's an accounting... It's an accounting discrepancy. It's a discrepancy, absolutely.（00:15:59–00:16:03） |
| proactivity | n. 主动采取行动、未雨绸缪；对应形容词 proactive | And since that person is, uh... I just think a little proactivity may be in order.（00:16:08–00:16:15） |
| letter of engagement | n. 委托协议／聘用函；此处律师服务协议，不是订婚信 | How would we proceed - if we decided to, uh... - Oh, well, this is a... Letter of engagement. It's very simple, straightforward.（00:16:58–00:17:07） |
| classy | adj. 有档次／有品位的（口语） | Okay, and the keyword here is "classy," all right? Super classy... Use only flowers that look expensive, but, you know, aren't.（00:18:37–00:18:45） |
| cop | n. 警察（口语）；call the cops 报警 | Where's the... Somebody call the cops! Don't call... don't call the police. Don't call the police.（00:19:47–00:19:50） |
| buck / grand | n. buck 美元（口语）；grand 一千元，后文 8 grand = 8,000 美元 | $500. 500 bucks?（00:20:22–00:20:28） |
| hooker | n. 性工作者（口语，带贬低意味） | The only way that entire car is worth 500 bucks is if there's a $300 hooker sitting in it.（00:20:47–00:20:53） |
| windshield | n. 汽车挡风玻璃（美式；英式 windscreen） | Now, let's talk about what you owe me for the windshield.（00:20:53–00:20:57） |
| do | n. 发型，hairdo 的简写；Nice do. 发型不错 | Brenda, looking good. Nice do.（00:24:13–00:24:17） |
| well-groomed | adj. 仪表整洁／打扮得体的 | Well-groomed, as always.（00:24:29–00:24:31） |
| meddle | v. 干涉／插手别人的事，常含不受欢迎之意 | You have meddled with the primal forces of nature, Mr. Hamlin, and I won't have it!（00:24:47–00:24:56） |
| measly | adj. 少得可怜／寒酸的（贬义） | A measly 26 grand?（00:25:24–00:25:28） |
| single-handedly | adv. 独自地／靠一人之力 | What Chuck did for this firm... And damn near single-handedly... 1/3 of this place belongs to him.（00:25:51–00:25:57） |
| thingumajig | n. 那个东西／叫不上名字的玩意儿（口语；原文复数） | You got five of these light thingumajigs? Uh, mm, 1, 2/3 are Chuck's.（00:26:02–00:26:09） |
| Danish | n. 丹麦酥皮糕点；此处不是丹麦人／丹麦语 | Yeah. Six... How many danishes... Six danishes? You can have all the Danish you want, Jimmy. No, no. They're Chuck's danishes, and Chuck isn't greedy, so h-he'll just take two...（00:26:09–00:26:18） |
| penny-ante | adj. 小额的／微不足道的（美式，贬义） | Until then, no more penny-ante checks designed to make it look like Chuck still works here.（00:26:25–00:26:30） |
| convey | v. 传达想法／意愿；convey wishes 传达意愿 | So, these are Chuck's own wishes that you're conveying?（00:26:35–00:26:39） |
| payroll | n. 工资发放体系／薪资名册；on payroll 仍由单位发工资 | His secretary's still on payroll.（00:27:02–00:27:03） |
| sabbatical | n. 较长的休假／休职期，常用于研修；不等于辞职 | If Chuck can call this an extended sabbatical, then so can we... He's that important to us.（00:27:03–00:27:08） |
| relatable | adj. 容易让人产生共鸣／亲近感的；此处赞美带讽刺 | You're so down-to-earth and relatable.（00:27:15–00:27:18） |
| atone | v. 赎罪／弥补过错，常用 atone for sth. | And you... Will... Atone!（00:27:19–00:27:24） |
| filings | n. 正式提交的文件；此处法院／案件相关文书 | I almost forgot... This month's filings. You could save me the postage.（00:27:43–00:27:48） |
| ground yourself | v. 让身体接地、释放静电；不是“禁足自己” | Ground yourself? Yes, I grounded myself.（00:31:20–00:31:25） |
| legal practice | n. 律师业务／律师事务所经营；不是法律练习题 | You do know I'm trying to start a legal practice, right?（00:32:50–00:32:52） |
| reimburse | v. 偿还某人垫付的费用；通常 reimburse sb. for sth. | Go ahead... Reimburse yourself.（00:33:12–00:33:14） |
| peaked | adj. 脸色不好、看着不舒服的（美式口语） | You look peaked.（00:33:28–00:33:30） |
| quicksand | n. 流沙；此处比喻论证基础不稳 | You proceed from false principles. Your argument is built on quicksand.（00:34:09–00:34:12） |
| liquidate a firm | v. 清算公司，把资产变现并处理债务／权益 | In order to pay out my share, suppose my partners are forced to liquidate the firm.（00:34:22–00:34:26） |
| crony | n. 密友／同伙；常暗含裙带关系或偏袒（贬义） | What happens to your cronies in the mailroom, the assistants, the paralegals, the janitorial staff?（00:34:35–00:34:40） |
| mailroom | n. 机构内收发信件、包裹的收发室 | What happens to your cronies in the mailroom, the assistants, the paralegals, the janitorial staff?（00:34:35–00:34:40） |
| paralegal | n. 律师助理，协助法律事务但不是执业律师 | What happens to your cronies in the mailroom, the assistants, the paralegals, the janitorial staff?（00:34:35–00:34:40） |
| janitorial staff | n. 保洁／建筑维护人员；janitor 管理、清洁楼宇的人 | What happens to your cronies in the mailroom, the assistants, the paralegals, the janitorial staff?（00:34:35–00:34:40） |
| pissant | adj./n. 蠢得可鄙／令人讨厌的（粗俗侮辱） | For the third time with these bull-crap contract counsel... - "Bull crap"? - Bull-crap, pissant P.D.（00:35:01–00:35:07） |
| arraignment | n. 正式宣读指控并要求被告答辩的庭审程序（美国法律） | I just had a case, Chuck, with three clients... Uh, arraignments, voir dire, jury trial...（00:35:12–00:35:18） |
| voir dire | n. 此处：陪审员遴选询问；法语来源法律术语 | Uh, arraignments, voir dire, jury trial...（00:35:16–00:35:18） |
| plasma | n. 血浆；sell plasma 卖血浆，不是等离子体 | Yeah, I might as well head down to skid row and sell plasma.（00:35:22–00:35:25） |
| reckoning / day of reckoning | n. 清算／面对后果；day of reckoning 不得不付出代价、面对现实的时刻 | I've been doing my damnedest, but the day of reckoning is here.（00:36:00–00:36:04） |
| stipend | n. 定期津贴／补助，不一定是工资 | A stipend... There's gonna be one every week. $857 from Hamlin, Hamlin, McGill?（00:36:26–00:36:31） |
| insistent | adj. 坚持不懈要求某事的；此处指坚持让对方接受钱 | I didn't want to take anything, but Howard was very insistent. And I'm gonna pay you back, too.（00:36:33–00:36:38） |
| recluse | n. 离群索居／不愿见人的人 | It's not like I'm a recluse.（00:36:40–00:36:43） |
| sarcasm | n. 讽刺／挖苦；minus the sarcasm 去掉讽刺的部分 | That's correct, minus the sarcasm.（00:36:55–00:36:57） |
| chump | n. 易受骗、被人利用的傻瓜（口语） | Hamlin's making you a chump!（00:36:57–00:36:59） |
| say-so | n. 某人一句话／指示；on sb.'s say-so 仅凭某人的话 | So I'm not supposed to use my name o... On Hamlin's say-so? What's he gonna do... Sue me?（00:38:15–00:38:22） |
| adversarial | adj. 对抗性的／双方相互敌对的 | Nobody wants to create an adversarial situation.（00:38:22–00:38:25） |
| matchbook | n. 纸板夹装的火柴；此处印有律师业务信息 | I'm sure Howard would gladly pay the cost of new matchbooks and so on.（00:38:25–00:38:29） |
| courtesy | n. 礼貌／礼节；professional courtesy 同业间的礼遇 | It's simply a matter of professional courtesy.（00:38:30–00:38:34） |
| stylistic | adj. 风格上的；a stylistic choice 风格选择，此处带自我开脱 | That sucked. We can call that a stylistic choice, I guess, - if you want to... - Hey, fellas.（00:39:52–00:39:56） |
| eerie | adj. 怪异、令人不安的／诡异的 | I know... Eerie, right.（00:40:01–00:40:05） |
| murder | n. 此处：极难熬的事（夸张口语），不是实际谋杀 | Winters in Cicero are murder.（00:41:09–00:41:11） |
| snot | n. 鼻涕（随意口语） | I'm talking cold that'll freeze the snot right in your nose.（00:41:16–00:41:20） |
| patch | n. 一小片区域；a patch of ice 一小片冰，不是补丁 | Soon as it was cold enough, he'd find a nice, smooth patch of ice.（00:41:48–00:41:53） |
| clear | v. 赚到／净得多少钱；clear 6, 8 grand 赚六千、八千 | Slippin' Jimmy had it dialed in, all right? One good fall... He'd clear 6, 8 grand.（00:42:09–00:42:15） |
| wrinkle | n. 新花样／新点子；此处不是皱纹 | The skateboard's a nice wrinkle... That makes it a year-round gig.（00:42:24–00:42:28） |
| gig | n. 一份活儿／赚钱的差事（口语；也可指演出） | The skateboard's a nice wrinkle... That makes it a year-round gig.（00:42:24–00:42:28） |
| discreet | adj. 不引人注意／低调的；此处拿夸张比喻反讽 | Nice boat. Yeah, discreet, like a stripper pole in a mosque.（00:43:06–00:43:11） |
| mosque | n. 清真寺（伊斯兰教礼拜场所） | Nice boat. Yeah, discreet, like a stripper pole in a mosque.（00:43:06–00:43:11） |
| stripper pole | n. 脱衣舞表演用的钢管（成人娱乐场所用语） | Yeah, discreet, like a stripper pole in a mosque.（00:43:08–00:43:11） |
| station wagon | n. 旅行车，后部带较大行李空间的轿车（美式） | I don't know. A station wagon? It's a Mercury, a 1988 Mercury Sable wagon.（00:43:15–00:43:21） |
| license plate | n. 汽车牌照／车牌（美式） | How does the license plate start? - 4. - 4.（00:43:33–00:43:36） |
| rattled | adj. 被吓到／慌乱、不安的；不是发出咔嗒声 | Now, once you've got her good and rattled, then you call for an ambulance, but really, you're calling for me.（00:44:19–00:44:25） |
| weed | n. 大麻（俚语）；此处 weed dealer，不是杂草 | I'm number one on your speed dial, right next to your weed dealer.（00:44:25–00:44:28） |
| hotfoot it | v. 急忙赶去（口语） | You call me. I hotfoot it over here. I just "happen" to be driving by.（00:44:28–00:44:32） |
| stomp | v. 跺脚／重重踩踏；此处演戏时跺脚制造气势 | Yell. Stomp. Call me a douche bag.（00:44:51–00:44:54） |
| razzmatazz | n. 花哨、热闹的表演／噱头；此处是演戏时的嘴上招数 | I'm gonna play it cool, give you back some of the razzmatazz.（00:44:54–00:44:57） |
| dinghy | n. 小艇；原句改写“水涨船高”的说法 | I'm the rising tide that raises all dinghies.（00:45:09–00:45:12） |
| embezzlement | n. 侵吞／挪用受托管理的钱财；不同于泛指偷窃 | The embezzlement case? Mm, yes, I'd... I'd be happy to talk it over.（00:45:49–00:45:55） |
| textbook | adj. 标准的／典型的；It was textbook. 完全按套路来的 | It was textbook, man. We were diamonds, but then she just took off.（00:48:08–00:48:12） |
| bail | v. 突然离开／溜走（口语）；此处不是支付保释金 | Okay, wait. She... She hit-and-run? That's what I'm saying. She bailed and wailed.（00:48:12–00:48:16） |
| felony | n. 重罪（美国法律分类）；不同于 misdemeanor 轻罪 | You fell into the honeypot, kid. You get it? Hit-and-run is a felony.（00:48:46–00:48:51） |
| mediate | v. 调解，帮助双方解决争端 | I can... I can mediate. It's... I represent their parents, so...（00:51:02–00:51:06） |

items.title: Chunks 收集箱
items.body:
# Chunks 收集箱

这里收集读到或想用的英语 chunks：搭配、短语动词、习语、话语套语、句式骨架等。**本页是候选池**；录入不表示用法已核实、已经编入 Book，或学习者已经掌握。

录入格式与去重规则见 [收集箱格式](../编纂与维护/Chunks 收集箱格式与录入规则.md)。以后在 English 项目中说“帮我录入”，由 Codex 在相应分类的表格中新增一行；网站只负责查看。例句格可附来源；没有例句时写“待补例句”，不阻止先收集。

## 常用搭配

| Chunk 原文 | 中文意思 | 例句 |
|---|---|---|
| pitch an offer | 推介一个报价／方案（商务语境；是否高频待核） | Your writer or team has to pitch an offer that better suits the requirements of the client than any of your competitors.（[商业提案写作资料](https://cdn2.hubspot.net/hubfs/41482/How%20to%20Write%20a%20Business%20Proposal%20Instructional%20Solutions.pdf)） |
| we had the benefit of ... | 我们得益于……；我们有……的便利／优势（原输入末尾为句点，后接内容待补） | 待补例句（用户提供片段；原出处未给） |
| all kinds of other things | 各种各样的其他东西／事情（概括前文之外的杂项） | 待补例句（用户提供片段；原出处未给） |
| core beliefs | 核心信念；根本相信的东西 | What are your core beliefs?（用户提供视频截图；原视频链接未给） |
| from my lens | 从我的视角来看（原输入 `from my lens.`；隐喻用法，表达时也可用更稳妥的 `from my perspective`／`through my lens`） | 待补例句（用户提供片段；原出处未给） |
| free speech | 言论自由 | Free speech matters.（教学自造） |
| aspire for ... | 渴望／追求……（可见于语料，但产出时优先用更常规的 `aspire to ...`；原句待核） | 待补例句（用户提供片段；[Cambridge aspire 词条与语料](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/aspire)） |
| have aspirations for ... | 对……怀有抱负／期望（名词 `aspirations` 的接法；与动词 `aspire to` 区分） | She had very high educational aspirations for her children.（[Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/aspiration)） |
| cautious optimism | 谨慎乐观；抱有希望但也看见风险 | We should approach the results with cautious optimism.（教学自造；[原访谈用语](https://www.hoover.org/plus/research/jensen-huang-vision-risk-and-gpu)） |
| wild-eyed optimist | 过分狂热／不切实际的乐观主义者（带评价色彩） | I'm a cautious optimist, not a wild-eyed optimist.（教学自造；[原访谈用语](https://www.hoover.org/plus/research/jensen-huang-vision-risk-and-gpu)；[wild-eyed 释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/wild-eyed)） |
| get the job done | 把任务完成；重点在结果（日常／工作；job 可以是具体任务，不一定是职业岗位；不自动表示完成得好。） | We will face challenges, we will confront hardships, but we will get the job done.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P002](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |
| no room for [X] | 没有容纳 X 的余地；某种态度或行为不应存在（中性／立场表达；可字面指空间，也可抽象表达不容许；no room for error 表示不允许出错。） | When you open your heart to patriotism, there is no room for prejudice.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P023](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |
| since our very founding | 自我们成立／建国之初以来（具体指代由语境决定；原例指美国建国。`since` 标记延续至今的起点，`very` 强调“最初、从一开始”，不是“非常”；可迁移到组织成立的语境。） | You know, the struggle for the soul of America since our very founding has always been an ongoing debate and still vital today.（[Joe Biden，2024-11-07 大选后全国讲话，官方实录](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |

## 短语动词与动词结构

| Chunk 原文 | 中文意思 | 例句 |
|---|---|---|
| turn out | 结果是；后来发现（此处只收结果／发现义） | It turned out that I was wrong.（教学自造；[Cambridge 释义](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/turn-out)） |
| go back to ... | 回到（某地／某话题）；追溯到（某时间／起点），具体义随宾语而变 | Let's go back to the main question.（教学自造） |
| live up to [an ideal/expectations] | 达到理想、承诺或期待的标准（中性；不是住在某地；常说 live up to expectations 或 live up to a promise。） | We've never fully lived up to that idea, but we've never walked away from it.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P012](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| settle for less | 接受更低的标准或次一等的结果；将就（日常／鼓励或评价；settle for 指接受不那么理想的选项；less 的比较标准由语境给出。） | Our journey has never been one of shortcuts or settling for less.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P007](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| see [someone] through [a difficult period] | 帮助某人撑过困难时期（中性；不是看穿某人；与 see through an excuse（识破借口）区分。原句包含 which 回指，不能把截取片段当完整句。） | which sees us through our darkest hours.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P022](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| let [someone] down | 让某人失望；辜负其期待（日常；此处不是物理上放下人；ever 强化原句的承诺。） | I will fight for you with every breath in my body, and I will never, ever let you down.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P017](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |

## 习语与固定表达

| Chunk 原文 | 中文意思 | 例句 |
|---|---|---|
| come onto your radar screen | 进入你的注意范围；开始被你留意 | When did it first come onto your radar screen?（[Washington State Oral History, p. 10](https://app.leg.wa.gov/oralhistory/pdf/OH864.pdf)） |
| on a first-principles basis | 从第一性原理出发；按基本原理推导（较正式；原输入 `on first principle basis`，此处显式校正） | We rebuilt the model on a first-principles basis.（教学自造；[搭配核查：American Academy of Actuaries, p. 4](https://www.actuary.org/sites/default/files/files/publications/LTC_Practice_Note_013119.pdf)） |
| swim upstream | 逆流而上；比喻逆势而行、顶着阻力做事（具体语境待核） | 待补例句（用户提供片段；原出处未给） |
| on the tip of one's tongue | 一个词／名字几乎想起、却暂时说不出来；截图中说某名字没有被顺口提起，属于较松的借用，不等于“经常被提及” | I know her - her name is on the tip of my tongue, but it won't come to me.（[Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/on-the-tip-of-tongue)；截图原句见用户提供视频，22:44） |
| the status quo | 现状；既有局面（原输入 `status quo.`；作名词时常带 `the`） | Certain people always want to maintain the status quo.（[Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/status-quo)） |
| make a difference | 起作用；带来积极改变（不是“制造一个差别”的逐词翻译） | What she showed is that one person can make a difference.（[Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/make-a-difference)） |
| in every possible way | 以一切可能的方式（原输入 `in every possible ways.`，`every` 后应接单数 `way`） | We tried to help in every possible way.（教学自造） |
| bring down the temperature | 缓和紧张局面；给争论降温（中性／公开讨论；这里的 temperature 是冲突强度，不是实际温度；说话时还需把前面的口语长句整理清楚。） | bring down the temperature.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P009](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| lay [something] to rest | 消除疑虑、结束争论，使某个问题不再反复被提起（中性偏正式；不等于每一种 solve；常配 doubts、fears、rumors、questions。原句用 lay to rest the question，宾语较长所以后置。） | I also hope we can lay to rest the question about the integrity of the American electoral system.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P010](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| keep the faith | 保持信心，别因受挫而放弃相信（鼓励／略带演讲色彩；faith 在此可指信心，不必指宗教；日常更直白可说 don't lose hope。） | And above all, we need to keep the faith.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| at one's own peril | 这么做会自担危险／后果；带警告（正式／郑重警告；比 at one's own risk 更带危险感，不宜用于每件小事。） | We lose these institutions of our government at our own peril.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P060](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| all talk and no action | 光说不做；只会嘴上说（日常／直接批评；带明确负面评价；评价同事时可能显得尖锐。） | We will no longer accept politicians who are all talk and no action, constantly complaining, but never doing anything about it.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |

## 话语套语

| Chunk 原文 | 中文意思 | 例句 |
|---|---|---|
| kind of | 有点；算是（口语中缓和或模糊表达，非“一种……”义） | It was kind of sad, really.（[Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english-thesaurus/kind-of)） |
| and so forth | 等等；诸如此类（列举末尾） | The patient can have apples, apple juice, apple sauce, and so forth.（[Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/and-so-on)） |
| The problem is ... | 问题在于……；引出真正的难点或障碍 | 待补例句 |
| It's all about ... | 关键在于……；重点全在……（具体依语境） | Success is all about networking.（[Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english-spanish/all-about)） |
| that's the thing about ... | 说到……，关键／麻烦就在这里（后文决定评价） | 待补例句 |
| Who wouldn't like that? | 谁会不喜欢呢？（反问，表示觉得它讨喜） | Who wouldn't like that?（用户提供；原出处未给） |
| Things are moving too fast. | 事情发展得太快了（可用于表达担忧或跟不上节奏；原输入小写开头） | Things are moving too fast.（用户提供；原出处未给） |
| Not that I know of. | 据我所知没有／不是这样（回答是非问题时，保留“我所知范围内”的余地；原输入小写开头） | “Is he married?” — “Not that I know of.”（[Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/not-that-i-know-of)） |
| win or lose | 不论输赢；输赢都一样适用（日常／口语与书面；可放句首或句尾补充条件；不是句式骨架 only when 的同义替换，而是把相反条件都纳入。） | And it can be trusted, win or lose.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P010](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| all kidding aside | 玩笑归玩笑，认真地说……（口语／对话与公开讲话；用来从玩笑切回认真话题；没有玩笑铺垫时不必硬用。原句后续 more ... as ... 是口语中的不整齐比较结构，不作为模板；这里只收话题切换词块。） | But, all kidding aside, I've never been more optimistic about America's chances in domestic and foreign policy as I am today.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P109](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| to state the obvious | 说句显而易见的话；这点不用说也知道（引出大家已知的事实，承认自己在强调常识；依语境可带轻微幽默或讽刺，不固定等于“说实话”。） | I know, for some people, it's a time for victory, to state the obvious.（[Joe Biden，2024-11-07 大选后全国讲话，官方实录](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |

## 句式骨架

| Chunk 原文 | 中文意思 | 例句 |
|---|---|---|
| how do we even ... | 我们到底要怎么……？（带困惑或难以置信的语气；待补完整结构） | 待补例句 |
| It never occurred to me to ... | 我从没想到要……（原输入 `occured` 已校正为 `occurred`） | It never occurred to me to ask.（[Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english-french/to-occur-to-somebody)） |
| we were just determined that ... | 我们当时就是认定／决意……（`that` 后接完整从句；原句与语境待核） | 待补例句（用户提供片段；原出处未给） |
| What's key about this is ... | 这里关键的是……（突出核心性质） | What's key about this is it's programmable.（用户提供视频截图，17:55；原视频链接未给） |
| It turns out (that) ... | 原来／结果……（以完整从句揭示后来发现的事实；原输入 `it turns out`） | It turns out we had the wrong address.（教学自造） |
| at the core of grit | 坚毅的核心在于……；原片段缺后文，具体含义待核 | 待补例句（用户提供片段；原出处未给） |
| we suffered our way here. | 我们一路吃苦才走到这里（具体所指待核） | We suffered our way here.（用户提供；原出处未给） |
| be determined to ... | 下定决心要……；不因困难而放弃（后接动词原形；不同于已收的 `determined that ...`） | I'm determined to get this piece of work done today.（[Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/determined)） |
| dedicated to ... | 致力于……（此处 `to` 是介词，后接名词或动名词；“献给／专供”是另一些语境） | She's completely dedicated to her work.（[Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/dedicated-to)） |
| It has to start from ... | 这得从……开始；提出论证或行动的起点（截图口语原句有自我修正） | It has to start from your core beliefs.（教学自造；据用户提供视频截图整理） |
| You could say that about ... | 这话也可以用来说……；同样的判断也适用于…… | You could say that about America.（用户提供视频截图；原视频链接未给） |
| aspire to be ... | 有志成为……；希望达到某种身份／状态（`to be` 后接名词或形容词） | As a child, he aspired to be a great writer.（[Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/aspire-to)） |
| You can't [do X] only when [Y]. | 你不能只在……的时候才……（用户中文提示）；批评把某种态度／行为限定在对自己有利的条件下。`can't` 表示“不应该／不能这样”，`only when` 限定条件；原例强调赢输都应爱国，不是“别等到赢了才爱国”。 | You can't love your country only when you win.（[拜登，2024-11-07 大选后全国讲话，官方实录第 1 页](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/pdf/DCPD-202400984.pdf)；拜登曾多次使用，用户具体记忆场次未确认） |
| make every [day/moment] count | 让每一天／每一刻都有价值；充分利用时间（日常与鼓励性表达；count 在此是有价值、产生作用，不是计数；不是 every 后可随意装任何名词的万能结构。） | Let's make every day count.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P020](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| I'd be surprised if [S V] | 如果……我会很意外；间接表示自己觉得那不太可能（日常与工作讨论；if 从句的肯定／否定决定预测方向；原句的 anything different 表示预计别人也听到相同担忧。） | I'd be surprised if you heard anything different than the concern about: Are we okay?（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P059](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| for all its faults | 尽管它有种种缺点，仍然……（评价／口语书面均可；for all 在此表达让步，不是为了全部；换对象时可用 for all his/her/their faults。原文 pass 后附官方 path 更正，照录。） | For all its faults though, American democracy remains the best pass [path; White House correction] forward to prosperity, possibilities, progress, fair play, equality.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P104](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| The real credit doesn't go to [X] | 真正的功劳不属于 X（而应归给别人）（感谢／评价与公开讲话；credit 是功劳、认可，不是贷款额度；原段下一句把认可给了听众。） | But the real credit doesn't go to me and my administration for the progress—for this progress.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P098](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| [X] is never a given | X 从来不是理所当然或自动有保证的（中性／论述；a given 作名词指可当成既定事实的东西；不能理解为过去分词被给予。） | greatness is never a given.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P007](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| The question is not whether [A], but whether [B] | 真正要问的不是 A，而是 B；重新界定讨论焦点（工作讨论／论述；whether A/B 可各接一个完整判断；不只是替换 but，而是在转移判定标准。） | The question we ask today is not whether our Government is too big or too small, but whether it works;（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P013](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| not out of [X], but because [Y] | 不是出于 X，而是因为 Y；澄清动机（口语书面均可／解释；out of 在此引出动机，X 常为情绪或态度名词，Y 为从句；不要照抄原政治主张。） | not out of charity, but because it is the surest route to our common good.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P014](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |

## 待分类与单词候选

| Chunk 原文 | 中文意思 | 例句 |
|---|---|---|
| all of that | 上述这些；那一切（回指前文，具体所指待核） | 待补例句 |

items.title: 总统演讲 Chunks：坚持原则、澄清判断与回应挫折
items.body:
# 总统演讲 Chunks：坚持原则、澄清判断与回应挫折

2026-10-08 首批：通读四篇 GovInfo 官方演讲后精选 20 个候选。原文例证按本地段号定位并逐字校验；提取片段会保留大小写、停顿和官方更正。场景迁移句均为教学自造。单篇或本批出现次数不等于英语总体频率。

原文合集见 [总统演讲原文合集](../原文与参考资料/原文、教材与影视/总统演讲原文合集：GovInfo.md)，数据见 `references/presidential-speeches/chunks.json`。它是采集与解释资料，尚未经过用户练习验证。

## 本批来源

- 2024-11-07 · 拜登：大选后的全国讲话 · [DCPD-202400984](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)
- 2023-09-28 · 拜登：民主与麦凯恩的遗产 · [DCPD-202300848](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)
- 2009-01-20 · 奥巴马：2009 年就职演说 · [DCPD-200900001](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)
- 2017-01-20 · 特朗普：2017 年就职演说 · [DCPD-201700058](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)

## Chunks 与使用边界

| Chunk | 中文意思与语气 | 原文例证 |
|---|---|---|
| bring down the temperature | 缓和紧张局面；给争论降温；中性／公开讨论。这里的 temperature 是冲突强度，不是实际温度；说话时还需把前面的口语长句整理清楚。 | bring down the temperature.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P009](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| lay [something] to rest | 消除疑虑、结束争论，使某个问题不再反复被提起；中性偏正式。不等于每一种 solve；常配 doubts、fears、rumors、questions。原句用 lay to rest the question，宾语较长所以后置。 | I also hope we can lay to rest the question about the integrity of the American electoral system.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P010](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| make every [day/moment] count | 让每一天／每一刻都有价值；充分利用时间；日常与鼓励性表达。count 在此是有价值、产生作用，不是计数；不是 every 后可随意装任何名词的万能结构。 | Let's make every day count.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P020](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| keep the faith | 保持信心，别因受挫而放弃相信；鼓励／略带演讲色彩。faith 在此可指信心，不必指宗教；日常更直白可说 don't lose hope。 | And above all, we need to keep the faith.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| win or lose | 不论输赢；输赢都一样适用；日常／口语与书面。可放句首或句尾补充条件；不是句式骨架 only when 的同义替换，而是把相反条件都纳入。 | And it can be trusted, win or lose.（[Joe Biden 2024-11-07 · P010](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202400984/html/DCPD-202400984.htm)） |
| live up to [an ideal/expectations] | 达到理想、承诺或期待的标准；中性。不是住在某地；常说 live up to expectations 或 live up to a promise。 | We've never fully lived up to that idea, but we've never walked away from it.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P012](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| at one's own peril | 这么做会自担危险／后果；带警告；正式／郑重警告。比 at one's own risk 更带危险感，不宜用于每件小事。 | We lose these institutions of our government at our own peril.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P060](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| I'd be surprised if [S V] | 如果……我会很意外；间接表示自己觉得那不太可能；日常与工作讨论。if 从句的肯定／否定决定预测方向；原句的 anything different 表示预计别人也听到相同担忧。 | I'd be surprised if you heard anything different than the concern about: Are we okay?（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P059](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| for all its faults | 尽管它有种种缺点，仍然……；评价／口语书面均可。for all 在此表达让步，不是为了全部；换对象时可用 for all his/her/their faults。原文 pass 后附官方 path 更正，照录。 | For all its faults though, American democracy remains the best pass [path; White House correction] forward to prosperity, possibilities, progress, fair play, equality.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P104](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| all kidding aside | 玩笑归玩笑，认真地说……；口语／对话与公开讲话。用来从玩笑切回认真话题；没有玩笑铺垫时不必硬用。原句后续 more ... as ... 是口语中的不整齐比较结构，不作为模板；这里只收话题切换词块。 | But, all kidding aside, I've never been more optimistic about America's chances in domestic and foreign policy as I am today.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P109](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| The real credit doesn't go to [X] | 真正的功劳不属于 X（而应归给别人）；感谢／评价与公开讲话。credit 是功劳、认可，不是贷款额度；原段下一句把认可给了听众。 | But the real credit doesn't go to me and my administration for the progress—for this progress.（[Joe Biden 2023-09-28 · P098](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202300848/html/DCPD-202300848.htm)） |
| [X] is never a given | X 从来不是理所当然或自动有保证的；中性／论述。a given 作名词指可当成既定事实的东西；不能理解为过去分词被给予。 | greatness is never a given.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P007](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| settle for less | 接受更低的标准或次一等的结果；将就；日常／鼓励或评价。settle for 指接受不那么理想的选项；less 的比较标准由语境给出。 | Our journey has never been one of shortcuts or settling for less.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P007](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| The question is not whether [A], but whether [B] | 真正要问的不是 A，而是 B；重新界定讨论焦点；工作讨论／论述。whether A/B 可各接一个完整判断；不只是替换 but，而是在转移判定标准。 | The question we ask today is not whether our Government is too big or too small, but whether it works;（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P013](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| not out of [X], but because [Y] | 不是出于 X，而是因为 Y；澄清动机；口语书面均可／解释。out of 在此引出动机，X 常为情绪或态度名词，Y 为从句；不要照抄原政治主张。 | not out of charity, but because it is the surest route to our common good.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P014](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| see [someone] through [a difficult period] | 帮助某人撑过困难时期；中性。不是看穿某人；与 see through an excuse（识破借口）区分。原句包含 which 回指，不能把截取片段当完整句。 | which sees us through our darkest hours.（[Barack Obama 2009-01-20 · P022](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-200900001/html/DCPD-200900001.htm)） |
| all talk and no action | 光说不做；只会嘴上说；日常／直接批评。带明确负面评价；评价同事时可能显得尖锐。 | We will no longer accept politicians who are all talk and no action, constantly complaining, but never doing anything about it.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |
| get the job done | 把任务完成；重点在结果；日常／工作。job 可以是具体任务，不一定是职业岗位；不自动表示完成得好。 | We will face challenges, we will confront hardships, but we will get the job done.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P002](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |
| let [someone] down | 让某人失望；辜负其期待；日常。此处不是物理上放下人；ever 强化原句的承诺。 | I will fight for you with every breath in my body, and I will never, ever let you down.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P017](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |
| no room for [X] | 没有容纳 X 的余地；某种态度或行为不应存在；中性／立场表达。可字面指空间，也可抽象表达不容许；no room for error 表示不允许出错。 | When you open your heart to patriotism, there is no room for prejudice.（[Donald Trump 2017-01-20 · P023](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-201700058/html/DCPD-201700058.htm)） |

## 从演讲迁移到日常（教学自造）

**1. bring down the temperature**

> Let's bring down the temperature and focus on what we can fix.（教学自造）

**2. lay [something] to rest**

> The new evidence should lay those doubts to rest.（教学自造）

**3. make every [day/moment] count**

> We only have a week left, so let's make every day count.（教学自造）

**4. keep the faith**

> It's been a difficult year, but I'm trying to keep the faith.（教学自造）

**5. win or lose**

> Win or lose, I'm glad we gave it a try.（教学自造）

**6. live up to [an ideal/expectations]**

> The product didn't live up to my expectations.（教学自造）

**7. at one's own peril**

> We ignore these warning signs at our own peril.（教学自造）

**8. I'd be surprised if [S V]**

> I'd be surprised if we finished this by Friday.（教学自造）

**9. for all its faults**

> For all its faults, this is still the tool I use most.（教学自造）

**10. all kidding aside**

> All kidding aside, I really appreciate your help.（教学自造）

**11. The real credit doesn't go to [X]**

> The real credit doesn't go to me; it goes to the people who tested it.（教学自造）

**12. [X] is never a given**

> Trust is never a given; you have to earn it.（教学自造）

**13. settle for less**

> We don't have to settle for less just because we're in a hurry.（教学自造）

**14. The question is not whether [A], but whether [B]**

> The question is not whether we can build it, but whether anyone needs it.（教学自造）

**15. not out of [X], but because [Y]**

> I asked not out of curiosity, but because I needed to make a decision.（教学自造）

**16. see [someone] through [a difficult period]**

> Her support saw me through a very difficult year.（教学自造）

**17. all talk and no action**

> He makes big promises, but he's all talk and no action.（教学自造）

**18. get the job done**

> It isn't perfect, but it gets the job done.（教学自造）

**19. let [someone] down**

> I know you were counting on me, and I'm sorry I let you down.（教学自造）

**20. no room for [X]**

> There's no room for personal attacks in this discussion.（教学自造）

## 跳过与边界

- `You can't love your country only when you win. / You can't love your neighbor only when you agree.`：收集箱已有同一 You can't ... only when ... 骨架；保留旧例句，邻居变体不重复计数。
- `What truly matters is not which party controls our Government, but whether our Government is controlled by the people.`：与本批 The question is not whether ... but whether ... 同属重新定焦动作；保留一条代表，此句留作变体。
- `Make America great again / America first`：依赖特定政治运动的口号；不适合作为日常表达的默认学习项。
- `not simply because ... but because ... / not only ... but ...`：常见对比与成对连接，已有一般性教材；本批优先选更有独立使用边界的表达。

最长保留项是“重新界定问题”的半固定骨架，完整原句仅作证据；不把整段政治论证当一个 chunk。演讲有正式、鼓动和郑重语气，日常使用时应按对象与场景调低力度。
